messages.author: 56b5225107e7c870
messages.subject: identifying point coordinates
parts:
I'd like to call ggplot2 from a Java application (via rJava), and then
invoke Java callbacks when the user clicks on a particular data point
in the plot. What is the best way to go about this?

Thanks,

ilya

messages.author: 0c39e60ddb38622b
messages.subject: Re: identifying point coordinates
parts:
Hi:

The Deducer package's PlotBuilder utility is a sort of 'interactive
ggplot2' that is used in conjunction with rJava, Perhaps a peek at its
source code would give you some useful pointers.

HTH,
Dennis

messages.author: 267c7c6c510dc8a2
messages.subject: Re: identifying point coordinates
parts:
No dice. ggplot2 does not contain the facility to map locations on the
graphics device to the data. If you are looking to do interactive
graphics within Java/R, look at the iplots package.

Ian
